prize_parts.citation: for developing empirical methods to estimate demand and competition in differentiated-product markets with endogenous prices, which made structural analysis of industries and policy counterfactuals possible

statement.case_for: I keep B047 as a single-achievement prize with Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes. Round 1 left my configuration's ballot and names intact but showed me that my citation should be narrower. The achievement is the identification and estimation of demand for differentiated products with endogenous prices and realistic substitution patterns (Berry 1994; Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes 1995). That is a compact, traceable discovery, and three decades of use in merger review, regulation, auctions, trade and health show it is a durable method. It also supplies a framework: it recovers markups and counterfactual policy effects from market data under explicit assumptions. In round 1 I wrote 'dynamic industries' into the citation. I now drop that phrase. Berry and Levinsohn are not credited for the dynamic-games line, and Hjalmarsson and Strömberg are right that a paper-anchored citation keeps the attribution clean. Pakes's dynamic-industry work remains part of why his share is substantial, but it need not be named in the citation. The chair asked how to compare B006 and B047 on how much a discovery changed how a field reasons. My answer is that both clear the bar, and B006 may have the wider reach across fields. B047 is ahead for me because the empirical record of its use is broader and more directly checked against outcomes such as merger retrospectives. Its credit also maps onto three specific people more tightly. The field has had no recent recognition, but I treat that as a minor tiebreaker and not as a ground of merit.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is unchanged. The three-name cap leaves out Bresnahan and Reiss, whose entry and market-structure work is a distinct and earlier tradition, and Benkard and Levin on dynamic estimation. Narrowing the citation makes the omission defensible but does not remove its cost. Structural IO results also depend on functional-form and equilibrium assumptions, so reported markups and merger effects can be sensitive to them. A two-name Kiyotaki-Moore award in B006 is a real competitor. It has a foundational mechanism and a clean core, and the 2008 crisis tested it. If the Committee reads B047 as a method rather than a discovery about the world, or weights breadth across fields over breadth of validated use, B006 could reasonably come first. My choice between them is a close judgement on weighting, not a claim of decisive difference in scientific quality. My knowledge rests on general background and not on verified citation data.

responses.point: Hassler's round-1 file prefers a three-name B006 with Kiyotaki, Moore and Gertler. He ties Gertler's credit to intermediary-frictions work with Kiyotaki and to quantitative financial-friction models, not to the accelerator papers that overlap with Bernanke's 2022 recognition. He asks that the citation say this explicitly.
responses.response: In round 1 I answered a two-name version of your proposal. That was a misreading of your file, and I now anchor on your three-name position. Separating Gertler's later intermediary work with Kiyotaki, which I recall as Gertler-Kiyotaki 2010 and Gertler-Karadi 2011 but have not verified, from the accelerator line is a coherent way to answer the overlap concern. It leaves a prize on the collateral and balance-sheet mechanism that I find more defensible than I did in round 1. I still weigh B047 slightly ahead, for two reasons. The empirical identification of the specific collateral channel is more mixed than BLP's applied record. And your own uncertainty list concedes that the boundary between recognisable and already-recognised work is blurry. If the Committee chose B006, I would want your explicit citation wording, which excludes bank-run and deposit-insurance themes.

responses.point: Krusell prefers B006 and ranks B047 second. He argues that collateral and financial-friction mechanisms are part of the shared core of macro, finance and policy modelling, whereas BLP's impact is concentrated in IO, antitrust and adjacent applied fields. He also says the omission of Bresnahan and Reiss is an attribution cost that B006 does not carry to the same degree.
responses.response: I accept the breadth-of-use point and think it is your strongest argument for B006. My reply is that influence beyond a home field is not the only measure of how much a discovery changed practice. BLP changed the daily working procedure of competition authorities, regulators and applied researchers, and that practice has been checked against outcomes in merger retrospectives. On Bresnahan and Reiss, I agree it is a real cost. Where I differ is that B006 also carries a cost from the cap, namely Gilchrist and the Gertler overlap, so I do not see the attribution comparison as one-sided. I have not treated your ranking of B047 second as support for it, and I would answer your breadth criterion by saying that it and mine are legitimate criteria that point to different candidates.

responses.point: Friberg ranks B006 first and B047 second. He describes my reason for ranking B006 third as accelerator overlap with the 2022 prize and lower novelty, and argues that the collateral mechanism changed how macroeconomists think about crises.
responses.response: I should clarify my own file. My reason for ranking B006 third in the opening was the thematic proximity to the 2022 prize and the mixed identification of the collateral channel, not a judgement that the work is less novel. The Kiyotaki-Moore mechanism is novel and foundational. Your distinction between the accelerator and the collateral-amplification mechanism, and your offer to accept a two-name fallback, make B006 a stronger alternative than I weighted it at the opening. I also note that you say you may over- or under-weight B047 because IO is your own field, and I have tried to apply the same maturity and attribution standards to both. We agree that neither is more 'scientific' in kind. I would still want the Committee to compare them on validated empirical record, where I think B047 has the edge.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson supports B047 with a narrow, paper-anchored citation on demand estimation with endogenous prices. She says Bresnahan-Reiss and Benkard-Levin are separable achievements and that adding them would turn a clean trio into a contested five- or seven-person award. She also says her view of B006 improved once Hassler framed a two-name version.
responses.response: I agree with the narrow citation and have adopted it in this round. I would add a candid limit to that argument. Narrowing the citation does not remove the omission cost. It only makes the omission a deliberate choice about what is being recognised and not an accidental gap. I agree that the Bresnahan-Reiss and Benkard-Levin lines are separable and should not be folded in. I would be cautious about your view that B006's empirical record is mainly theoretical validation plus model adoption. That may understate how the post-2008 literature used the mechanism, which I cannot judge in detail. On the chair's question, I do not think a two-name B006 would clearly overtake B047 for either of us, but it would be much closer than the opening rankings suggested.

responses.point: Teorell supports B047 and asks whether the Committee sees it as industrial organisation or as econometric methodology. He wants confirmation that the citation is for estimation methods and not for the whole field, and he notes that B047 has narrower opening support than B006 or B023.
responses.response: I think the distinction is real but less sharp than it first appears. BLP is an estimation method, and it also embodies a substantive account of how differentiated-product markets work: substitution patterns, markups and the response to policy. I would call it a method with a framework, and I would apply the same test to it as to any candidate, which is whether it recovered something about the world that could not be recovered before. My citation now says estimation of demand and competition, which is what you asked for. On the narrower opening support, I agree that it is information about how colleagues see the case and is not evidence of merit. I would welcome the Committee testing my view as a possible minority view, and I would move if the testing exposed a weakness in attribution or maturity and not just a disagreement over breadth.

responses.point: Strömberg supports B047 and notes that Pakes's share is arguably larger than the other two names' shares, which makes the attribution less symmetrical than it looks. He also argues that the committee should say openly that the citation recognises demand-estimation and dynamic-industry methods, not the whole empirical-IO tradition.
responses.response: Your asymmetry point is fair and I should have conceded it in round 1. Pakes's contribution spans the demand framework and the dynamic-industry work, while Berry and Levinsohn are credited for the demand core. Equal names in a citation do not imply equal shares, and I do not think that is a defect. Your preference to name the dynamic-industry methods, though, pulls against my narrowing. I now think the cleaner choice is to anchor the citation on demand estimation with endogenous prices, because the dynamic-games line also involves Benkard and Levin, who would then have an unavoidable claim under the cap. I agree that the Committee should say openly that the citation does not cover the Bresnahan-Reiss tradition.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee would regard the exclusion of Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin as a defect of the cap or as a legitimate consequence of a narrow, paper-anchored citation.
Whether a two-name or three-name B006 that is worded around collateral and balance-sheet amplification, and not the accelerator, would be judged distinct enough from the 2022 prize to outrank B047.

How sensitive headline structural-IO results, such as markups and merger counterfactuals, are to functional-form and equilibrium assumptions, and how that should be weighed against the mixed identification of the collateral channel.
Whether the Committee would see B047 as a substantive discovery or as a method, and whether that distinction should matter under the common criteria.
My assessments rely on general background knowledge, including the Gertler papers I name from recall. I have not verified citation, usage or attribution data independently.
statement.conflict_note: No connection to Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes or the other credited B047 names, nor to the alternatives B006 and B023, is documented in my supplied profile. My profile lists my main co-authors and collaborators (including Svensson, Ehlers, Erlanson, Martinello, Biró, Teytelboym and Trapp), and none of them is credited on a shortlisted ballot. I disclose, without adjudicating, my SSE affiliation alongside committee members Dreber Almenberg, Friberg and Strömberg, and a Lund connection with Enflo noted in her round-1 file. These are collegial affiliations and not candidate-related connections. My field of market and mechanism design is distant from structural industrial organisation, though auctions are an adjacent application area. I have tried to apply the same standards of attribution, maturity and demonstrated influence to every shortlisted field.
